mappings.note: Asks the reader to inspect a set of pictures and state what they share, i.e. draw an inference from supplied material. Content is artisan/handicraft labour, not this chapter's grandmother narrative, so no C-2.1/C-2.2 literature outcome applies; C-3.1 (analyses and evaluates the different audio and written material) is the only competency that covers reading supplied material rather than a literary text. Not C-3.2, which needs an argument with premises -- this only needs an observation.

Expository comparison of handmade against machine-made products. Again non-literary content, so the C-2.2 close-reading outcomes of this chapter cannot apply. C-3.1 rather than C-1.2: C-1.2 is a WRITING competency for composing in narrative/descriptive/expository styles from experience, whereas this is a 3-mark comprehension contrast drawn from a text the student read.

The operative question at the end of the stem is 'Do you think pot making is easy? If yes, why? If no, why not?' -- a judgement that must be justified from evidence in the text (trekking for clay, pounding it, shaping it). C-3.2 (argues with proper rationale by carefully evaluating premises) rather than C-3.1, because the yes/no-plus-reason form demands a defended position, not just analysis.
